newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Sept palm oil output seen up four pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Sept palm oil output seen up four pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in September was estimated to have risen by four percent to 843,000 tonnes over August, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Tuesday. He has previously estimated a rise of six percent.
Wong estimated end-Sept palm oil stocks at 905,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 800,893 tonnes at end-August.
He said palm oil exports in September were projected to be 645,000 tonnes from PORLA's 638,601 tonnes.
"The slowdown in seasonal palm production in September exceeded earlier expectation," Wong said in his latest report.

"As in August, the bulk of the increase was accounted by East Malaysia. In Peninsular Malaysia production was practically flat during the month with indications that the peak has tapered off." The absence of a promounced seasonal peak also suggests output will not drop sharply in the last three months of 1996.

With U.S. soya market registering extended losses in the last two weeks and CBSBO trading at a discount to crude palm oil last week for up to Dec shipment, it would be tough for palm oil to hold on to current levels in the next few weeks.
